submission.natural_language_explanation: Fires retrospectively on the bare-infinitive token 'be' acting as copula or passive auxiliary directly licensed by a preceding modal (will/can/could/would), negation (not/n't), or subjunctive/imperative licensor (let), i.e. the '[modal/not/let] be + predicative/passive complement' construction. It stays near baseline on finite copulas (is/are/was) in the same frames and on other bare infinitives (seem/feel/denote/have) after the same licensors, and changing the complement word after 'be' does not change its peak.
